attribution.note: Marcus directly endorses the adoption assessment.

semantics.note: Preserves the retrospective assessment and the distinction between sustained adoption and experimentation.

contract.note: Limited sustained use compared with experimentation is a fair ordinary reading. The contract appropriately distinguishes regular use from demonstrated retention.

evidence.note: The March–April six-country consumer survey measures usage frequency at one point, not retention of the same users over time.
Reported regular organizational use challenges a broad low-use interpretation, but the February–March survey does not establish deployment duration or lasting adoption.

reviews.rationale: Neither survey establishes sustained adoption or conversion from experimentation into lasting use. Low consumer frequency and substantial reported business use concern different populations and cannot settle the claim together.

attribution.note: Marcus directly states that GPT-5 remained absent.

semantics.note: Public nonrelease faithfully captures the statement, with July understood as the July 24 publication date.

contract.note: Reading the statement as public nonrelease of the named model is ordinary and preserves its date.

evidence.note: OpenAI's dated release history supports the July release chronology alongside contemporaneous reporting. The GPT-4o mini entry alone cannot establish GPT-5's nonrelease.
Contemporaneous July reporting describes GPT-5 as forthcoming and GPT-4o as the current release.
The August 2025 company launch disclosure concerns a later period and supplies chronology context only.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous reporting and the official July release chronology support GPT-5 remaining unreleased at the post date. The packet contains no contrary release record; the later launch is context only.

attribution.note: Marcus expressly endorses the retrospective confirmation of his earlier warnings.

semantics.note: The current assertion of confirmation is firm, even though several earlier warnings were hedged. The normalization captures that retrospective assertion.

contract.note: The five-component reading is fair, but restricting profitability to realized April–June net results adds a reporting period and accounting requirement Marcus did not supply. The other components remain assessable independently.

evidence.note: The reproduction of Leike's contemporaneous personal testimony supports continuing internal tensions, without establishing the other components.

OpenAI reports meaningful improvements in released vision and non-English text capabilities. This counters the plateau component, although it is company evidence and English text and coding reportedly remained comparable.
The company-disclosed prospective Apple integration suggests a distribution advantage but establishes neither an operating integration during the period nor a durable moat.

reviews.rationale: Internal tensions are supported; company-reported improvements in available capabilities contradict the plateau component. Adoption relative to valuation, profitability, and moat durability remain unresolved. This partial assessment does not depend on accepting the contract's unsupported quarterly profitability restriction.
